faq.a: Zeinab is associated with the Arabic form زَيْنَب, whose core sense is zeinab; a female given name.

faq.q: What is the origin of Zeinab?
faq.a: Zeinab is associated with Arabic. Zeinab is Arabic زَيْنَب (Zaynab), a well-established feminine name borne by members of the Prophet's family.
Yes — the underlying form زَيْنَب is Arabic.
Zeinab can occur in Muslim naming contexts, but it is better described as a Arabic-origin name used within some Muslim naming traditions than as an exclusively Islamic religious term.
Zeinab should not be classified as a Quranic personal name without a direct Quranic basis. Zaynab is not a Quranic personal name.

faq.q: What does Zeinab mean in Urdu?
faq.a: In Urdu, Zeinab is rendered زینب and carries the sense زینب (زنانہ نام).

faq.q: What does Zeinab mean in Persian?
faq.a: In Persian, Zeinab is rendered زینب and carries the sense زینب (نام زنانہ).
A romanized syllable approximation is zei-nab. No IPA transcription is asserted because a verified phonetic transcription was not available.

faq.q: What are the variants of Zeinab?
faq.a: Romanization variants include Zeinab, zeinab. Script forms are زينب, زَيْنَب, زینب, ज़ैनब.

faq.q: Is Zeinab a boy's or girl's name?
faq.a: Documented usage records this form as female. Gender is not inferred from the meaning of the word, and actual use may vary between communities.
